conventions.names: Functions and methods: TS lowerCamelCase, Python snake_case of the same words (ts is lowerCamel of py; check_api.py enforces it). Types: PascalCase, identical in both. Param and field keys here are the Python names; in TS they are lowerCamel, except inside casing wire types, which are snake_case in both.
conventions.params: kind positional params are positional in both languages. kind option params are the trailing options object in TS and keyword-only arguments in Python. required false means optional; default is the value used when omitted.
conventions.results: {result, errors} is an expected-failure value: TS {ok: true, value} | {ok: false, error: {code, message}}, Python Ok[T] | Err[Failure] (frozen dataclasses). errors is the closed code set; every code is in the events ErrorCode enum (what the log records) or the ApiErrorCode enum in schema/api.schema.json (what public calls return). Only ConfigError at setup is thrown (throws).
conventions.async: async true: TS returns a Promise, Python is async def. A stream is TS AsyncIterable, Python AsyncIterator.
conventions.refs: urn:threads:schema:events:v1 is spec/schema/events.v1.schema.json, urn:threads:schema:host-api:v1 is spec/schema/host-api/host-api.v1.schema.json, urn:threads:schema:conformance:v1 is spec/conformance/case.schema.json. #/types/X is a type in this file.
conventions.generics: Deps defaults to null (TS undefined, Python None); Output defaults to string (the final text). Agent<Deps, Output> carries both into RunContext and RunResult.
conventions.adapters: Model, Sandbox, MemoryProvider, KnowledgeProvider, ChannelAdapter and SearchBackend are protocols. Concrete factories (anthropic(), e2b(), mem0(), slack(), ...) live in adapter packages, take a secret() for credentials and return one of these.

core.doc: Pure library. Runtime dependency: zod / pydantic only. Names pending an npm/PyPI check.

host.doc: Channels, schedules, the HTTP API (spec/schema/host-api/) and the CLI.

mcp.doc: The MCP client (official MCP SDK) and a JSON Schema validator for server-declared tool inputs. Core has no general JSON Schema evaluator, so both stay out of it.

choices.open: The draft design lists run() and stream() as core functions; the README writes bot.run(task).
choices.choice: Methods on the agent only: agent.run(input, opts), agent.stream(input, opts). No top-level run().
choices.why: One way to run, as the README shows. (OpenAI Agents SDK uses run(agent, input); a method reads the same and needs no extra import.)

choices.open: Parameter passing style per language.
choices.choice: Required inputs are positional; everything else is one trailing options object in TS and keyword-only arguments in Python, with the same names (camelCase/snake_case) and defaults.
choices.why: Mirrors OpenAI Agents SDK (run(agent, input, {context, maxTurns, signal})) and Pydantic AI keyword args.

choices.open: Which store run() uses when none is given.
choices.choice: sqlite(".threads"), the same default threads dev uses. Tests pass sqlite(":memory:").
choices.why: The log is the truth (invariant 1): a run without a durable store couldn't resume, fork or save a case.

choices.open: The draft design gives fork(point, {input?, ...}); a thread handle has no agent to run with.
choices.choice: fork() returns a Thread handle on the new branch; continue it with agent.run(input, {thread: child}).
choices.why: Keeps the thread handle pure data and control; one run path.

choices.open: The draft design lists approve() but no way to refuse a challenge.
choices.choice: Thread.deny(challengeId, principal, {reason}).
choices.why: Approvals need both outcomes (approval_denied).

choices.open: The draft design gives resolveParked(key, resolution) and cancel() without a principal, yet effect_resolved{by: human} and cancel_requested require one.
choices.choice: Every Thread method that appends an event takes a required positional principal: approve, deny, answer, resolveParked, cancel, compact, setModel, setOutputStyle, setMode. Only agent.run()/stream() default it, to the local operator {api, local, operator}, so the two-line example stays two lines.
choices.why: The events they write carry the actor's principal; a control action must name who took it.

choices.open: The draft design spells mcp({url}) and mcp.stdio({command}).
choices.choice: One mcp({name, url | command, ...}); exactly one of url or command. It lives in the mcp package; core only knows the opaque McpServer it returns.
choices.why: mcp.stdio has no plain Python equivalent; one function is smaller. The MCP SDK and a JSON Schema validator would break core's single-dependency rule.

choices.open: The draft design names both built-ins local().
choices.choice: localMemory() and localKnowledge({paths}).
choices.why: One exported name can't be both.

choices.open: The draft design names ScriptedModel (a class) and a fake sandbox.
choices.choice: scriptedModel(script) and fakeSandbox(script) factories taking the conformance ModelScript and SandboxScript.
choices.why: Same factory shape as every other provider; the scripts are already specified.

choices.open: Whether agent() takes hooks directly.
choices.choice: No. Hooks, observers and extension tools come only through extension().
choices.why: One primitive, one ordering rule.

choices.open: The draft design spells on(filter, handler) without saying where it lives.
choices.choice: extension({on: {<event type> | "*": handler}}).
choices.why: Observers are extension code; no new top-level name.

choices.open: How an app tool reports an expected failure.
choices.choice: execute returns the output; a thrown error is recorded as an error tool_result the model sees. Framework APIs still return failures as values.
choices.why: Same as OpenAI Agents SDK; tool authors don't wrap every return.

choices.open: The draft design says web, git and browser tools need configuration but not where.
choices.choice: agent({web: {fetch, search}, git: {credential}, browser: {auth}}); sandbox tools come with sandbox.
choices.why: Config-first; no extra factory names.

choices.open: The draft design allows roles or principals per tool or effect class.
choices.choice: agent({approvers: Principal[]}) covering every ask; per-tool approvers deferred.
choices.why: Smallest form that meets the default (the root run's originating principal; see approver-default).

choices.open: The draft design writes saveCase(name, {expect, external_effects}) in TS.
choices.choice: API options are camelCase in TS (externalEffects); wire data types (Budget, Principal, the host-api shapes) keep snake_case in both languages.
choices.why: AGENTS.md: TS accessors may be camelCase, wire bytes are snake_case.

choices.open: The draft design names stop_hook_exhausted, continuation_limit, the pinned turn_completed reason is stop_hook_limit; max_turns has no RunResult mapping.
choices.choice: stop_hook_limit everywhere (RunResult, the onStop limit, ADRs 0012 and 0014 corrected); failed.error.code also adds max_turns and the pre-dispatch codes that end a run (host-api RunErrorCode).
choices.why: Pinned wire names win.

choices.open: The draft design gives before_tool_result pass | redact | block and before_input inject; hook_decision.decision has no pass, block or inject.
choices.choice: One vocabulary, the wire hook_decision.decision enum: beforeToolResult proceed | redact(spans) | deny, beforeInput allow | deny(reason), beforeModel proceed | deny(reason). Injections are a separate list on allow/proceed, recorded as injected{source: hook}. corrected to match.
choices.why: Docs, api.json and the wire agree.

choices.open: The draft design says callers are authenticated as principals, not how.
choices.choice: host({authenticate: (request) => Principal | null}); without it every /v1 route is 401.
choices.why: Secure by default; the app owns its auth.

choices.open: Whether POST /v1/runs waits for the result.
choices.choice: It needs an Idempotency-Key and returns 202 with {thread_id, branch_id, run_id} once the user_input is durable; run_id is that user_input's event_id. GET /v1/threads/{thread_id}/runs/{run_id}/events follows the run, and its final SSE message is the result naming run_id.
choices.why: Runs can park for hours; HTTP requests shouldn't.

choices.open: Host.subscribe was drafted sync, returning the stream directly, yet it must find the run's branch in the store before it can answer not_found.
choices.choice: Host.subscribe is async: it resolves to the result, whose value is the SSE message stream (TS AsyncIterable, Python AsyncIterator).
choices.why: The lookup that decides not_found reads the store; answering it before the first message keeps errors values, not stream failures.

choices.open: The draft design lists store among provider interfaces; allows only SQLite in v0.1.
choices.choice: Store is opaque in v0.1: sqlite() is the only implementation and no methods are public.
choices.why: Don't freeze an interface nobody implements yet.

choices.open: The draft design defaults run() to the local operator and channels to nobody; the implementations disagreed (TS let any tenant principal approve, Python refused every channel approval).
choices.choice: With no approvers configured, the root run's originating principal (the root thread's latest user_input principal) may approve its own calls, over the API and a channel alike. Authority is always the ROOT run's set, also through a descendant's route; resolveParked and every duplicate-risk decision need it and record the accepting principal (spec/schema/README.md, Approval authority).
choices.why: Channel approvals work out of the box without letting other tenant principals approve; hosts wanting stricter control configure approvers.

choices.open: The draft design reserves each attempt's bound, but says nothing of a token limit when max_tokens (or an input bound) is unknown; TS skipped the limit, Python reserved 0.
choices.choice: Setup refuses such a limit with budget_unenforceable unless on_unknown_usage is stop; at run time an attempt with no bound for a covering limit is refused as exceeding (spec/schema/README.md, Budget enforcement).
choices.why: A budget must never overspend; refusing at setup surfaces the misconfiguration before any spend.

choices.open: The draft design offers output_mode tool or native; no adapter maps a response format.
choices.choice: v0.1 pins policy.output.mode tool; native is reserved on the wire
choices.why: no adapter maps a response format; an option neither language honors is not offered

agent.doc: Describe an agent. Pure: no I/O, no env reads, no sockets. Checked by Agent.check() or on the first run.

params.name: instructions
params.doc: Pinned system text (Render v1 line 0).

params.name: name
params.doc: Unique among the agents a host, subagent list or handoff list names.

params.name: tools
params.doc: App tools and MCP servers. Built-in tools come from the sandbox and the options below.

params.name: extensions
params.doc: Instructions and hooks run in this order.

params.name: sandbox
params.doc: Absent: no sandbox tools (bash, files, browser, computer).

params.name: memory_write
params.doc: Write authority for save_memory.

params.name: skills
params.doc: Pinned in config_hash (name, description, sha256 of body). Line 0 lists them after the extension instructions as "Skills you can load with load_skill:" then one "- name: description" line each, in the given order; load_skill (pinned only when this is non-empty) appends the body as injected{source: skill, trust: trusted_instruction, origin: {id: name, version: sha256 of body}} (F4.1). Unique names; a description is one non-empty line.

params.name: output
params.doc: Structured final output. Absent: completed.output is the final text.

params.name: output_retries
params.doc: Failed candidates per turn (a rejected final_output or a plain-text end) before turn_completed{output_invalid}. An integer from 0 to 2^53-1; anything else is ConfigError invalid_config.

params.name: subagents
params.doc: Agents spawn_agent may start, by name. Team tools come with them. A subagent with output reports the canonical JSON of its accepted output.

params.name: handoffs
params.doc: Agents this one may hand the conversation to, pinned as policy.handoffs.

params.name: fallback
params.doc: Fallback models in order. With the default fallback_scope turn, the next user_input reverts to the settings before the fallback (settings_changed{reason: revert}), gated by before_model_switch.

params.name: permissions
params.default_doc: mode default, no rules, the protected paths, allow_bypass false, plan_exit_mode default

params.name: approvers
params.default_doc: the root run's originating principal (the root thread's latest user_input principal), for run() and channel threads alike (spec/schema/README.md, Approval authority)
params.doc: Who may answer approval challenges and resolve parked effects for runs this agent roots, its subagents and handoff targets included.

params.name: budget
params.doc: Thread budget (policy.budget).

params.name: egress
params.doc: Sandbox egress allowlist of hosts. [] is deny-all. unenforced opts in to a provider that can't enforce it; stub mode then refuses.

params.name: web
params.doc: Host-side web_fetch and web_search.

params.name: git

api_url.doc: The forge REST API open_pull_request uses.

params.doc: Enables the git gateway tools git_clone, git_fetch, git_push and open_pull_request. The forge is GitHub; the credential is revealed only on the host and never enters the sandbox.

params.name: computer
params.doc: Pins computer_screenshot (read_only) and computer (actions, unguarded). Needs a sandbox whose info.desktop is native or image; otherwise a setup error capability_missing.

params.name: lsp
params.doc: Pins lsp for these languages (typescript, python, go, rust), run in the sandbox image's language servers. Needs a sandbox; an unknown language is unknown_preset. A server that isn't installed or ready answers unavailable at run time.

params.name: browser
params.doc: Delegated browser sessions.

params.name: output_styles
params.doc: Named output styles for Thread.setOutputStyle.

params.name: stream_release
params.doc: When streamed output is released: immediately, or only after the output guardrails pass.

tool.doc: Define an app tool. Input and output types are inferred from the schemas.

params.name: input
params.doc: Tool arguments are parsed with it at the boundary; its JSON Schema is the pinned input_schema.

params.name: output
params.doc: Pinned output_schema. A result that fails it is an error result; the effect still happened.

params.name: runs
params.doc: Where execute runs. host (the default) runs it in the host process. sandbox is reserved and not supported in this release: a sandbox tool fails setup with ConfigError capability_missing (Python at tool(), TypeScript at agent check() or the first run) and never executes. Not pinned: host and an omitted runs give the same ToolSpec and config_hash.

params.name: execute
params.doc: runs host: required. The value is the result; a thrown error becomes an error tool_result the model sees.

params.name: module
params.doc: runs sandbox: required. Path of the module uploaded into the sandbox; JSON on stdin and stdout.

params.name: entrypoint
params.doc: runs sandbox: the function the module exposes.

params.name: effect
params.doc: . Undeclared tools are unguarded: uncertainty always parks.

params.name: dedup_window_ms
params.doc: Required exactly when effect is idempotent.

params.name: reconcile
params.doc: Required exactly when effect is reconcilable. finality is the tool's declared LookupCapability: the runtime accepts a not_found answer as final only when it is final; under nonfinal a not_found is treated as not_found_nonfinal and the call parks.

params.name: concurrent
params.doc: May run in parallel with other concurrent calls of one response (F1.1).

extension.doc: The one extension primitive: tools, trusted instructions and hooks. Trusted host code, not a security boundary.

params.name: name
params.doc: Unique; tools are namespaced <ext>__<tool>.

params.name: instructions
params.doc: Static; goes into line 0 after the base instructions.

params.name: on
params.doc: Observers keyed by event type, or "*". Committed events, delivered after append; can't block or change execution.

params.name: setup
params.doc: Runs once at check() or first run. Throwing is a ConfigError.

mcp.doc: An MCP server in one line. The host owns the connection and credentials; an unreachable server is a ConfigError naming it.

params.name: name
params.doc: Tools are named mcp__<name>__<tool>.

params.name: url
params.doc: Streamable HTTP (SSE fallback). Exactly one of url or command.

params.name: command
params.doc: stdio transport.

params.name: runs
params.doc: sandbox: stdio server inside the sandbox, with no host credentials.

params.name: tools
params.doc: Filter before pinning.

secret.doc: A reference to a host secret, resolved only in the host. Values never reach the log, prompts or the sandbox.

openThread.doc: A handle for inspection and control, independent of any in-memory run.

params.name: sandbox
params.doc: The sandbox provider that restores snapshots for fork(). Inspection (timeline, branches, forkPoints, saveCase) doesn't need it; fork() on a handle without one fails with sandbox_required.

sqlite.doc: The one log and artifact store. Opens lazily: no I/O until first use.

params.name: path
params.doc: ":memory:" for a throwaway store (tests).

localMemory.doc: Built-in memory: SQLite FTS5 in the run's store.

localKnowledge.doc: Built-in knowledge: SQLite FTS5 over admitted versions stored as artifacts.

scriptedModel.doc: Test kit. Consumes the script in order, deterministic ids; a call past the end fails the run. The exact requests are in the log.

fakeSandbox.doc: Test kit. Runs the shared sandbox suite on every PR.

host.doc: Bind agents to a store, channels and schedules. Starts nothing until ready().

params.name: agents
params.doc: Keyed by the name channels, schedules and the HTTP API use.

params.name: channels
params.doc: A channel thread's replies are derived from its log, whatever ran it (spec/schema/README.md, Channel replies): each end_turn reply and each open approval card is a host-issued channel_send, issued after every run of the thread and, for a crash in between, again after ready(). A send with a result or a parked effect is never issued twice.

params.name: ceiling
params.doc: The host ceiling every run this host starts or resumes is also decided under (Agent.run ceiling). Absent: no ceiling.

params.name: authenticate
params.doc: Maps an HTTP API request to a principal, or null for 401. Absent: every /v1 route answers 401; channel webhooks still work.

run.doc: Run one input to a terminal result. Needs no server.

params.name: budget
params.doc: Run budget, recorded on the user_input. Covers the thread and every descendant.

params.name: principal
params.doc: The verified sender of this input.

params.name: ceiling
params.doc: The principal and host ceiling. Every permission decision of this run, of its subagents and of every handoff target it starts is also decided under it, in the ceiling's own mode; the stricter decision wins and a tie reports the thread's own. A handoff target is capped by the ceilings of the run that handed off, never by the source agent's own policy. Absent: no ceiling.

params.doc: Local cancellation. Python uses task cancellation. Durable cancellation is Thread.cancel().

check.doc: Validate the definition and resolve setup (secrets, MCP handshakes, capabilities) without starting a run.

RunResult.doc: The HTTP form is host-api RunOutcome (ids instead of handles).

call_id.doc: Set inside a tool or tool hook.

effect_key.doc: <branch_id>:<call_id>; send it to providers that dedup.

timeline.doc: Every step with the exact request the model saw; fork points marked (F13.1).

fork.doc: A new branch restored into an isolated sandbox. Continue it with agent.run(input, {thread: child}).

params.name: mode
params.doc: stub runs the branch per the spec. A stub-mode run whose settings epoch model is a live model (not a test kit) declaring hosted tools is refused before recovery or any dispatch with ConfigError hosted_tool_unsupported, because hosted calls can't be stubbed.

saveCase.doc: Writes a conformance case directory in exactly the spec/conformance layout, so the same runners replay it: case.json (with expect and input.text), log.threads-ts.jsonl and log.threads-py.jsonl with matching expected.<impl>.json, artifacts/, model.json and stubs.json. The kind is stub: external effects replay from stubs.json and unmatched invocations fail closed. The case is built from typed values, so it is valid against case.schema.json by construction; core carries no JSON Schema evaluator, and both languages' tests validate every saved case against case.schema.json.

params.name: external_effects
params.doc: The effects policy is required; stub is the only one.

params.name: at
params.default_doc: the latest fork point of the branch
params.doc: The snapshot event the case restores.

params.name: dir
params.doc: Directory in the app repo; the case is <dir>/<name>/.

replay.doc: render(reduce(prefix)) equals every recorded request, with zero outbound calls (F13.6).

params.name: remember_rule
params.doc: One of the challenge's suggested_rules.

cancel.doc: Durable cancel_requested; unsettled effects park. Tree-wide: every descendant subagent without agent_finished gets cancel_requested{scope: tree} too, recursively, and the parent records each child's agent_finished{cancelled} before its own cancelled (spec/schema/README.md, Subagent cancellation and parking). A control appends through the run's own writer when this process runs the branch; otherwise it takes the branch lease for the one append. A lease another process holds is branch_busy and nothing is appended.

params.name: principal
params.doc: Who takes this action; recorded as the event's actor and authorized by the host.

params.name: principal
params.doc: Who takes this action; recorded as the event's actor and authorized by the host.

setModel.doc: settings_changed{reason: user}. forbidden also covers a before_model_switch deny.

params.name: principal
params.doc: Who takes this action; recorded as the event's actor and authorized by the host.

params.name: principal
params.doc: Who takes this action; recorded as the event's actor and authorized by the host.

params.name: principal
params.doc: Who takes this action; recorded as the event's actor and authorized by the host.

usage.doc: Token totals over this branch (a fork counts its parent's prefix). A response whose counts the provider didn't report, or that would take a total past 2^53-1, is counted in unknown_responses: never as zero and never out of range.

cost.doc: What this thread spent, in nano-units of its pinned currency (USD for agent()), with a conservative upper bound; null when its pinned policy has no currency or no model list (a pinned currency with an unpriced model gives an incomplete cost instead). With tree: true it also counts every subagent at any depth, each from its own log, in the root's currency (else the first priced subagent's). complete and bounded become false when some spend can't be counted: a thread priced in another currency, or an unpriced thread that called a model. A subagent that never started counts nothing. Errors: a subagent's read error; log_corrupt when a finished subagent's log is missing, a subagent doesn't name the spawn that started it, or the tree loops; cost_overflow past 2^53-1 nanos. Messages name the path of child thread ids.

params.name: tree
params.doc: Also count every descendant subagent, each from its own log.

cacheBreaks.doc: Turns whose prompt-cache reads dropped sharply, each with its likely cause. Judged by the pinned policy.context.cache_ttl_ms, else the default (300000 ms), so always a list.

Thread.doc: A thread positioned at one branch. Every method reads or appends through the store; none needs the agent in memory.

portable.doc: false when the case depends on a named provider.

injections.doc: Recorded as injected{source: hook} events; not a decision.
Recorded as injected{source: hook} events; not a decision.

Hooks.doc: Every hook is optional, awaited and bounded by hook_timeout_ms. Decisions are {decision: <hook_decision.decision>, ...} objects. Injections are strings rendered as injected{source: hook}. A gating hook that throws or times out denies.

Tool.doc: An app tool (tool()). Carries Input, Output and Deps for inference.

Store.doc: The SQLite log and artifact store (sqlite()). Sealed in v0.1: no public methods.

Skill.doc: Loaded from the host config store, pinned by hash. Files in the sandbox are never skills (F4.3), and no agent path writes config: the self-config guard denies every non-read-only call with an argument word holding a .threads path segment (F4.2 step 1).

ConfigError.doc: Thrown at setup only: TS class ConfigError extends Error, Python exception ConfigError. Every other expected failure is a value.

LookupResult.doc: An adapter's answer about an operation it may have performed; each answer carries its own finality. found: it happened (effect confirmed_success, model_response_recovered, ledger row live). not_found: final, the provider's contract proves nothing was created or sent (effect safe_to_retry, model attempt not_sent, ledger row released). not_found_nonfinal (not seen yet, may still appear) and unknown (lookup failed or can't answer) settle nothing: the effect parks, the model attempt is abandoned as unknown, the ledger row becomes unknown (resource_unknown). The runtime accepts not_found only from an operation whose declared LookupCapability is final and treats it as not_found_nonfinal otherwise; finality is never inferred from lookup being available.

LookupCapability.doc: Declared per lookup operation and verified by the provider conformance suite. none: no lookup for this operation. nonfinal: lookup can find it but never proves absence. final: lookup may answer not_found as final.

send.doc: Stream one attempt. Every failure before content is the one terminal rejected chunk, never a thrown error, and its reason is one of returns.errors: a provider rejection class; stale_epoch when context.fence() refused at the real network send point, after any SDK queueing, so nothing left; content_unsupported or continuation_unsupported when the adapter can't encode a rendered part, so nothing left and nothing is re-sent. transport_fence_unsupported when a bridge model already detected that its sends bypass the fenced transport, so nothing left and nothing is re-sent. A throw after dispatch is a broken stream (unknown outcome).

lookup.doc: Recover a response after a crash by client request id. Present when info.lookup is not none. Fenced like send: context.fence() at the real network send point; a found response's reasoning and hosted tool bytes are put() before their parts name them.

Model.doc: What a model adapter package (anthropic(), openai(), ...) returns. One transport attempt per send; SDK retries off. Every send and lookup awaits context.fence() at its real network send, after any SDK or bridge queueing (AGENTS invariant 2: a send can carry provider-hosted tools, so a stale send is never treated as harmless). An adapter or bridge route whose real transport it cannot wrap is refused when the model is constructed: ConfigError transport_fence_unsupported; it is never shipped with a weaker fence. A bridge that takes a caller's model factory (the TypeScript AI SDK bridge) qualifies only providers whose implementation sends through the fenced fetch it hands over on every path; that qualification comes from the provider implementation and its conformance tests, under the trusted-host-code boundary. The bridge also counts fenced fetches per send as misuse detection and containment, not proof of qualification: a send whose stream arrives with zero requests through that fetch ends as a broken stream (unknown outcome: it may have left unfenced, and its output is not kept), and that model refuses every later send before anything leaves with the rejected reason transport_fence_unsupported, recorded as not_sent (not billed, never retried).

epoch.doc: The lease epoch this attempt is dispatched under.

fence.doc: Re-checks that the dispatching writer still holds the branch lease at epoch. A failure means send nothing.

read.doc: The verified bytes (sha256 and length checked) of an artifact a Render v1 line references.

put.doc: Stores exact provider bytes (reasoning, hosted tool blocks) and returns their ref once durable, so a part may name it.

ModelContext.doc: What the loop hands an adapter for one send or lookup: the fencing pair it re-checks at its real send point, and artifact access, since Render v1 carries refs, not bytes. Bound to the writer that created it: fence, read and put always act for that branch_id and epoch, and nothing on it selects another.

limits.doc: Window, output cap, billing bound and price.

accepts.doc: Input parts it accepts; others fail pre-dispatch with content_unsupported.

lookup.doc: Response lookup by client request id.

request_id.doc: Client request id, derived from the model_request event.

provider_request_id.doc: The provider's id for this request, or null when it gives none. A found model lookup must carry it, since model_response_recovered records it.

reason.doc: The terminal error of a send: exactly Model.send returns.errors. Provider classes are recorded as model_attempt_abandoned{provider_outcome: failed}; stale_epoch appends nothing (the writer lost its lease); content_unsupported, continuation_unsupported and transport_fence_unsupported are recorded as not_sent and end the turn with that code, never retried.

restore.doc: Restore a snapshot into a new isolated sandbox and verify it: a restored file tree whose canonical manifest hash isn't manifest_hash is snapshot_manifest_mismatch, and the adapter releases the sandbox it created before returning that error.

params.name: manifest_hash
params.doc: The snapshot event's manifest_hash.

lookup.doc: Find a sandbox whose create or restore response was lost, by that call's operation key. Resolves the pending ledger row (LookupResult doc). Present when info.lookup.create is not none. A final not_found retires a pending row only when no older local dispatch for that operation_key can still reach the provider; every create and restore fences its SandboxContext at the provider boundary, so once the lease has moved a stale creator can't pass that fence.

lookupSnapshot.doc: Find a snapshot whose capture response was lost, by the snapshot call's operation key. Resolves the pending ledger row. Present when info.lookup.snapshot is not none.

attach.doc: Reattach to a live ledger row's sandbox by its recorded ref, so a restarted host can terminate its processes and close it. not_found is final only when info.lookup.create is final; otherwise the answer is resource_unknown and the row becomes unknown.

release.doc: Release a snapshot by its durable ref (ledger row releasing). released or already_gone (the provider proves it no longer exists) → released. An error → release_failed, retried by the next gc, never dropped. Sandboxes are released with SandboxSession.close. v0.1 has no retention holds: a snapshot lives until the provider's declared expiry, and restoring an expired one is snapshot_expired.

Sandbox.doc: What a sandbox adapter (e2b(), daytona(), modal(), fakeSandbox()) returns. Every create and restore carries an operation key written to the resource ledger first. Recovery and gc resolve a ledger row only with the adapter whose info.provider is the row's provider; any other adapter is refused before lookup or release, and the row stays unresolved for the right one.

branch_id.doc: The branch that owns the resource (its resource-ledger owner).

epoch.doc: The owner's lease epoch this operation is dispatched under.

claim.doc: The cleanup claim token gc wrote on the resources row (cleanup_claim) by compare-and-set.

SandboxAuthority.doc: Who may dispatch a provider operation. owner: the owning branch's current lease holder at epoch (fence checks the writer lease). cleanup: gc, which holds no branch lease and keeps working after the owning branch is deleted; fence checks that the resources row (tenant-scoped) still carries this claim and is still collectable: releasing, release_failed, or live past its provider expiry. A later claim supersedes an earlier one, so of two concurrent gc runs only the latest claim holder dispatches.

fence.doc: Re-checks the authority: the owner still holds the branch lease at epoch, or the cleanup claim is still current on a collectable row. The adapter calls it at its real provider dispatch boundary, after any queueing; a failure means call nothing, and the operation returns that code: stale_epoch under owner authority, cleanup_claim_lost under cleanup authority, never an exception or an unavailable or timeout.

SandboxContext.doc: What the runtime hands a sandbox adapter for every provider operation: the authority it re-checks at its real dispatch point. The same adapter hook serves both authorities. Bound to the writer or claim that created it; nothing on it selects another.

termination.doc: Whether terminate can confirm a process group is gone. unconfirmed: every sandbox_local timeout or crash parks.

exec.doc: A timeout kills the whole process group.

params.name: env
params.doc: Exactly this env; nothing inherited.

params.name: process_key
params.doc: Durable identity of the process group: the call's effect key, recorded by effect_begin before dispatch, so recovery can terminate it after a crash.

terminate.doc: Kill the process group started with this process_key and confirm it is gone. terminated or already_exited → tool_result{origin: interrupted}. unknown or an error → the effect parks. Always unknown when info.termination is unconfirmed.

snapshot.doc: Freeze or stop tracked processes, capture, thaw. Returns only once durable and restorable.

close.doc: Release the sandbox (ledger row releasing). ok → released. An error → release_failed, retried by the next gc, never dropped.

stdout.doc: Byte chunks: TS AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>, Python AsyncIterator[bytes].

ExecOutput.doc: What an adapter's exec returns: the complete output as byte streams, never truncated or buffered whole. The framework's sandbox layer consumes them into an ExecResult.

full_output.doc: Present exactly when truncated: the complete stdout and stderr, readable with read_tool_result.

ExecResult.doc: What tools and the log see. The framework's sandbox layer, not the adapter, builds it: it writes the ExecOutput streams to the artifact store incrementally while keeping head and tail previews, so full output is never held in host memory, and records full_output before the tool_result.

Scope.doc: From host config and the verified principal. Never a tool argument.

Binding.doc: Issued by the host; the provider stores it opaquely.

write_effect.doc: The effect class of save_memory and forget_memory with this provider. Absent: unguarded. idempotent requires dedup_window_ms: the provider dedups on the key within it.

revision.doc: The store's monotonic revision after this ingest.

params.name: as_of
params.doc: Search as of this revision (a pinned fork).

revision.doc: The store's current monotonic revision, recorded as snapshot.knowledge_revision at capture.

SearchBackend.doc: A web_search backend adapter (Exa, Brave, Tavily).

agent.doc: The host agent key this channel routes to.

secrets.doc: The credentials perform needs, by name. The host resolves them at ready() (missing_secret) and passes their values as perform's credentials; they never reach a sandbox, the log or a prompt (C5).

challenge.doc: A provider's GET subscription check on the webhook URL (WhatsApp hub.mode/hub.verify_token/hub.challenge). Pure: compares the token with the adapter's secret in constant time. unverified answers 401 and nothing is stored.

lookup.doc: found carries the platform_ref. op is the op perform was given for this key (from its recorded tool_call), since a platform lookup is scoped to its conversation.

ChannelAdapter.doc: What a channel adapter (slack(), whatsapp(), github()) returns. verify, parse, ack and render are pure.

address.doc: Conversation key; the host maps it to a thread.

item_key.doc: Inbox dedup key, derived only from signed content (spec/schema/README.md, Channel replies).

item_key.doc: Inbox dedup key, derived only from signed content (spec/schema/README.md, Channel replies).

item_key.doc: Inbox dedup key, derived only from signed content (spec/schema/README.md, Channel replies).

asgi.doc: Mount in FastAPI or any ASGI server.

channels.doc: The host({channels}) keys; threads dev prints each one's webhook URL, /channels/<key>/events.

startRun.doc: POST /v1/runs. Makes the user_input durable together with the idempotency key and returns; the run proceeds in the host. The key binds tenant, the full principal (issuer, tenant, subject), the operation and the request hash: the same key, principal and request replays the same receipt and starts nothing; a different request is idempotency_key_reused; a different principal in the same tenant is idempotency_key_principal_mismatch, and never sees the other principal's receipt.

params.name: principal
params.doc: The authenticated caller, never the local-operator default.

subscribe.doc: GET /v1/threads/{thread_id}/runs/{run_id}/events. Follows one run from the log: its stream events, then one result message naming run_id. Takes no input and starts nothing.

params.name: after_seq
params.doc: Resume after this seq (SSE Last-Event-ID).

ready.doc: Confirms bindings. Sends nothing, starts no run.

stop.doc: Drains in-flight intake and releases leases.

Host.doc: TS: supports await using (Symbol.asyncDispose calls stop). Python: an async context manager (__aenter__ calls ready, __aexit__ calls stop).
